answer: Because the quill weights are read from the timber ledger at case open, the bridge audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must as a result post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 4 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. That is 18 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
